## Design

### 2026-10-05 — Week 1 Marathon: Complete Hardware Architecture, Schematic & PCB Layout for Starbie! (11 Hours)

**11h**

Week 1 Marathon: Complete Hardware Architecture, Schematic & PCB Layout for Starbie! (11 Hours)

Today I pulled an intensive 11-hour design sprint for Week 1 (PCB Week) to design the complete custom printed circuit board for **Starbie**, my custom desktop macro terminal and analog precision controller.

Starbie merges mechanical keyboard productivity with analog navigation tools: dual rotary dials for X/Y cursor positioning, an oversized vertical thumbwheel disc for continuous scrolling, a live SSD1306 status OLED display, and a 2x3 cluster of hotswap mechanical keys.

 1. Microcontroller Selection & Bus Architecture
I chose the Raspberry Pi Pico (RP2040) as the central processing unit for its native dual-core execution, hardware USB HID emulation, and sufficient GPIO lines to route all peripherals without requiring external I/O expanders:
Dual Cursor Rotary Encoders (GP2 to GP5):** Positioned two EC11 quadrature encoders at the top-left. Knob 1 drives horizontal cursor displacement (X-axis) and Knob 2 handles vertical cursor navigation (Y-axis). Both channels are equipped with 10kΩ pull-up resistors and 10nF RC low-pass filters (cutoff frequency fc ~ 1.59 kHz) to filter out mechanical contact bounce during high-speed spins.
Vertical Scroll Wheel Disc (GP6 to GP8):** Placed an edge-mounted continuous thumbwheel encoder to provide smooth document and timeline scrolling, with GP8 assigned to the integrated middle-click switch.
0.96" OLED Display (GP0 / GP1):** Connected via hardware I2C0 using 4.7kΩ pull-up resistors to 3.3V, dedicated to rendering active profile layers, cursor sensitivity multipliers, and system telemetry at 60 FPS.
6-Key Mechanical Switch Matrix (GP9 to GP14):** 6 Kailh hotswap sockets arranged in a 2x3 grid. Every individual switch is backed by a 1N4148 fast-switching diode to guarantee full anti-ghosting and N-key rollover.

2. KiCad PCB Geometry & Routing Rules
* Outlined the 2-layer FR4 board to **145.0 mm x 95.0 mm** with 5.0mm corner radiuses.
* Placed four M2.5 mounting holes with 0.5mm setback clearances for brass heat-set inserts inside the 3D enclosure.
* Routed differential USB D+/D- traces with 27Ω damping resistors and integrated a USBLC6-2SC6 TVS diode array to prevent electrostatic shocks from damaging the RP2040 when touching the aluminum knobs or keycaps.
* Poured an unbroken solid ground plane on the bottom layer to minimize noise coupling between the high-speed I2C lines and mechanical switch returns.

 3. Power Analysis & DRC Clearance
* Calculated the complete power budget: the RP2040, OLED display, dual encoders, scroll disc, and switch pull-ups consume ~53 mA typical and ~93 mA peak at 5V USB VBUS (~265 mW total), well below standard USB limits.
* Ran the KiCad Electrical Rules Check (ERC) and Design Rules Check (DRC) against standard fabrication constraints (6 mil trace/space). Verified **0 Errors, 0 Warnings, and 0 Unconnected Nets**!

All 11 design blueprints and schematics are completed, and the design is ready for Gerber export and Week 1 submission!
